title_en: Supreme People's Court Measures for the Management of People's Jurors (For Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Procedural Rules for the Management of People's Assessors (For Trial Implementation)

Fa Fa [2005] No. 1

Chapter I General Provisions

Article 1 These Procedural Rules are formulated in accordance with the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Improving the System of People's Assessors (hereinafter referred to as the Decision) and the Implementing Opinions of the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice on the Selection, Training, and Assessment of People's Assessors (hereinafter referred to as the Opinions), for the purpose of properly managing people's assessors and ensuring the implementation of the people's assessor system.

Article 2 People's courts at all levels shall establish a steering group for the work of people's assessors to guide the management of people's assessors.

The management of people's assessors includes the personnel management of people's assessors and the day-to-day management of their participation in trial activities.

Article 3 The personnel management of people's assessors shall be the responsibility of the political work department of the people's court.

The political work department shall establish a non-permanent body or designate a dedicated person to be responsible for the personnel management of people's assessors.

Article 4 The day-to-day management of people's assessors' participation in trial activities shall be handled by a specific department designated by the people's court based on actual circumstances.

Chapter II Determination of the Number of Assessors

Article 5 A basic people's court shall, taking into account factors such as the number and characteristics of cases within its jurisdiction, the population size, geographical area, and ethnic composition, and also considering the need for higher people's courts to randomly select people's assessors from its pool, propose an opinion on the number of people's assessors, which shall be not less than one half and not more than the full number of currently serving judges of the said court, and submit such opinion to the standing committee of the people's congress at the corresponding level for determination.

Article 6 Before submitting the opinion on the number of people's assessors to the standing committee of the people's congress at the corresponding level for determination, the basic people's court shall first report it to the next higher people's court for review. The next higher people's court may make appropriate adjustments to the number of people's assessors within its jurisdiction.

The higher people's court shall report the numbers of people's assessors of all basic people's courts within its jurisdiction to the Supreme People's Court for recordation.

Article 7 The number of people's assessors may be adjusted based on actual circumstances. Such adjustments shall be made in accordance with the procedures for determining the number of people's assessors.

Chapter III Selection and Appointment

Article 8 The selection and appointment of people's assessors shall be conducted within the determined number of assessors.

Article 9 The basic people's court shall, one month before the commencement of the selection and appointment work, publicly announce to the community matters such as the number of people's assessors to be selected, the selection conditions, the period for recommendations (applications), and procedures, so that relevant entities may recommend candidates and citizens may submit applications.

When necessary, the basic people's court may encourage citizens to submit personal applications, or encourage the entities where citizens work, or the grassroots organizations where their household registration or habitual residence is located, to recommend candidates for people's assessors.

Article 10 The entity where a citizen works, or the grassroots organization where their household registration or habitual residence is located, may recommend such citizen to the local basic people's court for appointment as a people's assessor only after obtaining the citizen's consent.

A citizen may directly submit an application to the basic people's court where their household registration or habitual residence is located to serve as a people's assessor.

Article 11 The basic people's court shall require the relevant entity recommending a people's assessor, or the citizen submitting an application, to provide copies of the identity documentation of the recommended person or applicant, and to fill out and submit three copies of the Recommendation Form for Candidates for People's Assessors (Appendix 1) or the Application Form for Candidates for People's Assessors (Appendix 2).

The Recommendation Form for Candidates for People's Assessors and the Application Form for Candidates for People's Assessors shall be in the format and content prescribed by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 12 The basic people's court shall examine the citizens who are recommended or who have personally applied to serve as people's assessors, in accordance with Articles 4, 5, and 6 of the Decision and Article 2 of the Opinions. The examination shall primarily cover the authenticity of the information filled in the Recommendation Form for Candidates for People's Assessors or the Application Form for Candidates for People's Assessors, as well as the qualifications, work ability, and daily conduct of the recommended person or applicant.

Article 13 The basic people's court shall submit the list of initially determined candidates for people's assessors, together with the Recommendation Form for Candidates for People's Assessors or the Application Form for Candidates for People's Assessors, to the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the corresponding level for comments.

If the basic people's court deems it necessary to investigate the relevant circumstances of a recommended person or applicant, it shall, together with the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the corresponding level, conduct an investigation at the entity where the citizen works, or at the grassroots organization where their household registration or habitual residence is located.

Article 14 The basic people's court shall determine the candidates for people's assessors based on the results of the examination and its number of people's assessors.

When determining candidates for people's assessors, attention shall be paid to including individuals from different industries, genders, age groups, and ethnic backgrounds.

Article 15 No citizen may serve as a people's assessor in more than one basic people's court at the same time.

Article 16 The basic people's court shall report the determined candidates for people's assessors to the next higher people's court for review. The next higher people's court shall primarily review the qualifications of the candidates for people's assessors.

Article 17 Candidates for people's assessors that have been reviewed shall be submitted by the president of the basic people's court to the standing committee of the people's congress at the corresponding level for appointment.

When submitting a request to the standing committee of the people's congress at the corresponding level for the appointment of people's assessors, the basic people's court shall provide the following materials: the proposal for appointment of people's assessors, the Recommendation Form for Candidates for People's Assessors or the Application Form for Candidates for People's Assessors, and other materials as required by the standing committee of the people's congress at the corresponding level.

Article 18 The basic people's court shall send a copy of the list of appointed people's assessors to the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the corresponding level, and shall report it level by level to the higher people's court for recordation, and at the same time publicly announce it to the community.

The basic people's court shall promptly notify in writing the appointment decision to the individual people's assessor, the entity where they work, and the grassroots organization where their household registration or habitual residence is located.

Article 19 The basic people's court shall issue a People's Assessor Work Certificate to each people's assessor.

The People's Assessor Work Certificate shall be uniformly designed by the Political Department of the Supreme People's Court, and the courts in various localities shall print it themselves.

Chapter IV Training

Article 20 Training for people's assessors is divided into pre-service training and specialized training in trial work during their term of office.

Before taking up their posts, newly appointed people's assessors shall receive training in the trial knowledge and skills necessary for performing their duties. This includes the duties and rights of judges, judicial ethics, trial discipline, judicial etiquette, basic legal knowledge, and basic rules of procedure.

During their term of office, people's assessors shall, based on the actual needs of their jury work, receive specialized training in trial work. This primarily covers mastering the general rules for evaluating evidence, finding facts, and applying laws, and studying new laws and regulations.

Article 21 The education and training administrative department of the Supreme People's Court and the National Judges College shall be responsible for formulating a unified training outline and training materials for people's assessors, setting clear training and teaching requirements, and regularly supervising and inspecting the training of people's assessors. When necessary, they may hold model training classes for people's assessors and training classes for trainers of people's assessors.

Article 22 The education and training administrative departments of higher people's courts and the judicial training institutions shall be responsible for planning the training of people's assessors within their respective jurisdictions and related management and coordination work, and shall undertake the tasks of pre-service training for people's assessors within their jurisdictions.

Article 23 If conditions permit, the education and training administrative departments of intermediate and basic people's courts and judicial training institutions may, when entrusted by the higher people's court, undertake the tasks of pre-service training for people's assessors.

Intermediate people's courts shall be responsible for reviewing and approving the teaching plans for specialized training in trial work for people's assessors during their term of office within their jurisdictions.

Article 24 The basic people's court shall, together with the judicial administrative department of the people's government at the corresponding level, promptly submit the list of individuals to undergo pre-service training and the training opinions to the education and training administrative department and judicial training institution of the higher people's court.

Article 25 Training for people's assessors shall be conducted based on the actual needs of people's assessors in performing their duties and in conjunction with jury practice. The specific content of the training shall be tailored to the requirements of different trainees.

Article 26 Training for people's assessors shall be conducted through a combination of centralized full-time training and on-the-job self-study. Alternatively, training may be conducted in sections or by accumulating hours, as appropriate to the actual situation.

In addition to centralized lectures, training formats may include court observation, thematic seminars, and other methods.

The in-person teaching time for pre-service training shall generally be no less than 24 class hours, and specialized training in trial work during the term of office shall be no less than 16 class hours per year.

Article 27 People's courts shall provide venues, facilities, and other necessary conditions for people's assessors to participate in training.

Article 28 People's courts shall issue a Certificate of Completion to people's assessors who have successfully completed pre-service training.

For pre-service training of people's assessors conducted by the National Judges College, the Certificate of Completion shall be verified and issued by the education and training administrative department of the Supreme People's Court and the National Judges College.

For pre-service training of people's assessors conducted by training institutions of higher people's courts or entrusted to training institutions of intermediate or basic people's courts, the Certificate of Completion shall be verified and issued by the education and training administrative department of the higher people's court and the relevant training institution.

The Certificate of Completion for pre-service training of people's assessors shall be uniformly printed by the Political Department of the Supreme People's Court.

Chapter V Assessment and Commendation

Article 29 The basic people's court, together with the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the corresponding level, shall assess the performance of duties by people's assessors.

The assessment of people's assessors shall combine routine assessment with annual assessment.

Article 30 The assessment of people's assessors shall include aspects such as their work performance in jury service, ideological and moral character, work attitude, trial discipline, trial conduct, and participation in training.

Where an intermediate people's court or a higher people's court randomly selects people's assessors from the list of people's assessors of the basic people's court in the city where it is located to participate in the trial work of the selecting court, such court shall notify the respective basic people's court of the performance of duties by such people's assessors at the selecting court, which shall serve as one of the bases for assessing the people's assessors.

Article 31 The assessment results shall serve as the basis for commending and rewarding people's assessors.

The basic people's court shall promptly notify the assessment results in writing to the individual people's assessor. If a people's assessor has objection to the assessment results and applies to the basic people's court for review, the basic people's court shall accept the application.

Article 32 People's assessors who have made outstanding achievements or have other notable contributions in trial work shall be commended and rewarded by the basic people's court together with the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the corresponding level.

Article 33 The basic people's court shall promptly notify in writing the decision to commend and reward a people's assessor to the individual people's assessor, the entity where they work, and the grassroots organization where their household registration or habitual residence is located.

Chapter VI Removal from Office

Article 34 Where a people's assessor falls under any of the circumstances provided for in Article 17 of the Decision, the basic people's court shall, together with the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the corresponding level, conduct an investigation and verification.

If the circumstances are verified to be true, the president of the basic people's court shall submit a request to the standing committee of the people's congress at the corresponding level to remove the people's assessor from office.

Where a people's assessor falls under any of the circumstances listed in subparagraphs (1), (2), or (3) of Article 17 of the Decision, the personnel management department for people's assessors of the basic people's court where the assessor serves shall conduct the investigation and verification in accordance with the regulations. If during the investigation and verification, it is discovered that the people's assessor falls under the circumstances listed in subparagraph (4) of Article 17 of the Decision, the matter shall be referred to the discipline inspection and supervision department of the said court for investigation and verification.

Article 35 Where a people's assessor commits any act listed in subparagraph (4) of Article 17 of the Decision, which does not yet constitute a crime, in addition to being removed from office as a people's assessor in accordance with the law, the basic people's court may, when necessary, propose in writing that the entity where the assessor work impose disciplinary sanctions in accordance with relevant provisions.

Article 36 The term of office for a people's assessor is five years. Upon the expiration of a people's assessor's term, their office is automatically terminated. The basic people's court need not submit another request to the standing committee of the people's congress at the corresponding level for removal from office.

Article 37 Where a people's assessor is removed from office, the basic people's court shall notify in writing the removed individual, the entity where they work, and the grassroots organization where their household registration or habitual residence is located.

The basic people's court shall send a copy of the list of removed persons to the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the corresponding level, and shall report it level by level to the higher people's court for recordation, and at the same time publicly announce it to the community.

Chapter VII Subsidies and Funds

Article 38 The various subsidies to which a people's assessor is entitled during the performance of duties shall be paid promptly by the people's court in accordance with the regulations.

Article 39 Expenses incurred by a people's assessor for public transportation, meals, etc., due to participation in trial activities or training, shall be subsidized by the court where they serve, with reference to the local standard for travel expense reimbursement.

For a people's assessor with no fixed income, during the period of participation in trial activities or training, the court where they serve shall provide a subsidy for each actual working day, with reference to the average monetary wage level of local employees in the previous year.

Where a people's assessor participates in trial activities of an intermediate people's court or a higher people's court, the intermediate people's court or higher people's court that randomly selected the people's assessor to participate in the trial activity shall provide the various subsidies to the people's assessor in accordance with the preceding two paragraphs.

Article 40 If a people's assessor who has a work unit is subjected to a reduction or disguised reduction of their wages, bonuses, or other welfare benefits by their work unit due to participation in training or trial activities, the basic people's court shall promptly propose corrective measures to the work unit, or the competent authority of the work unit, or the superior authority of the work unit.

Article 41 The subsidies to which people's assessors are entitled for participating in training and trial activities, and the expenditures necessary for the people's court to implement the people's assessor system, shall be included by the people's court in the current year's operational budget and promptly reported to the financial department of the people's government at the corresponding level for appropriation, and shall be guaranteed by the government finance at the corresponding level.

People's courts at all levels shall keep separate accounts, separate management, and earmark funds for all expenditures related to the implementation of the people's assessor system, in order to ensure the effective implementation of the people's assessor system.

Chapter VIII Supplementary Provisions

Article 42 The procedures for the management of people's assessors in maritime courts, Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps courts, railway courts, and other specialized courts shall be formulated separately.

Article 43 These Procedural Rules shall be interpreted by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 44 These Procedural Rules shall come into effect on the date of promulgation.

Appendices: 1. Recommendation Form for Candidates for People's Assessors (omitted)

2. Application Form for Candidates for People's Assessors (omitted)
